messages:
incident-bot: [P1] Dedicated-pool node degradation — 'vortex-dedicated-01'. Auto-page to oncall. Affected tenant: VortexSys (enterprise, VPC). Symptoms: increased generation latency, ~3% request failures, partial KV-cache misses. Detected: provider signaled preemptive host maintenance causing 2 nodes to become NotReady (gpunode-27, gpunode-28).

emma_oncall: I’m on it. Confirming impact windows and routing. tagging @olivia_support + @tom_cs to prep customer comms.

emma_oncall: Quick triage: host events show provider 'preemptive maintenance' at 11:23 UTC, nodes were evacuated and then failed health checks. nvlink warnings + ECC counters rising on gpunode-27 before eviction.

miguel_sre: ETA on replacement nodes from autoscaler?

emma_oncall: Autoscaler spun up two replacements but they are still provisioning (image + drivers). We’ve temporarily routed VortexSys traffic to fallback policy: model -> redwood-small-quantized (same family, lower throughput) to preserve availability. Latency up ~120ms p50 -> p95 spikes.

jia_eng_runtime: Can we force immediate placement on on-demand hosts instead of spot for this pool? For enterprise VPCs we should prefer on-demand.

emma_oncall: Yes. Doing: 

```
# switch burst nodes to on-demand for this pool
dedpoolctl update --pool vortex-dedicated-01 --burst-mode on-demand --reason "preemptive host maintenance"
dedpoolctl drain-node --pool vortex-dedicated-01 --node gpunode-27 --reason "preemptive host reboot"
dedpoolctl drain-node --pool vortex-dedicated-01 --node gpunode-28 --reason "preemptive host reboot"
```

emma_oncall: Started drain commands. Also enabling warm cache on replacements.

miguel_sre: Good. Please capture kernel logs and NV logs for both nodes before we decommission. Add to the incident ticket. Use: 

```
# grab diagnostics
ssh root@gpunode-27 'sudo dmesg | tail -n 200' > gpunode-27-dmesg.txt
ssh root@gpunode-27 'nvidia-smi -q' > gpunode-27-nvidia-smi.txt
smartctl -a /dev/nvme0n1 > gpunode-27-nvme.txt
```

miguel_sre: If ECC counters are rising, we might trigger hardware replacement vs firmware update.

olivia_support: I’ll draft a customer-facing note. Suggested: "We detected degraded capacity in your dedicated pool due to provider-initiated host maintenance affecting a subset of GPUs. We routed your traffic to a fallback model to maintain availability; engineers are replacing impacted nodes and prioritizing on-demand capacity. We will follow up with an RCA." OK to send now?

emma_oncall: Send with a brief ETA: replacement nodes expected in ~15–25m. Call out that no data was accessed outside the VPC; tenant isolation preserved.

tom_cs: Also let VortexSys know we’re prioritizing their reserved burst to on-demand and won't bill them for degraded requests during remediation window. I'll confirm with billing.

jia_eng_runtime: Observed a backlog in the router for this pool — some sessions timed out on initial fallback. I’m bumping worker concurrency on the fallback service for that tenant: 

```
service scale redwood-small-quantized --replicas 4 --tenant VortexSys
```

devops_oncall: Provider case opened: ticket #CLOUD-87654321 — they acknowledge scheduled maintenance but said eviction was earlier than advertised. Asking for host list and replacement timeline.

emma_oncall: Current status: drains in progress, replacements provisioning (2 on-demand), fallback routing active, customer notified (draft approved), provider engaged. Impact: approx 3% of requests returned 503 during 11:22–11:30 UTC; now down to <0.5% with fallback.

miguel_sre: Plan of record: 1) complete drain + rotate out bad hardware 2) keep VortexSys on on-demand for next 24h, 3) collect full diag artifacts and upload to incident ticket, 4) run post-replace validation (smoke gen + latency tests).

emma_oncall: Assigning follow-ups: 
- miguel_sre: hardware diag + RCA draft (owner)
- jia_eng_runtime: router/backpressure tuning + performance validation
- olivia_support/tom_cs: customer comms and billing note
- devops_oncall: cloud provider follow-up and CAPEX ticket if HW replacement required

miguel_sre: Kicking off diag collection now, will attach artifacts to incident board. If ECC thresholds > X within counters we'll request physical replacement.

olivia_support: Sent outbound message to VortexSys SOC + primary contact at 11:33 UTC. Copy of message: "We're actively mitigating a dedicated pool capacity event affecting a subset of your GPUs. We've routed traffic to a fallback model and are provisioning on-demand replacements. No customer data left your VPC. We'll provide hourly updates and an RCA after root cause analysis."

emma_oncall: Noted. Please add the incident link and expected next update at 11:50 UTC.

devops_oncall: Provider says replacement hosts will be ready in ~18 minutes. They are providing a list of affected host IDs. I'll correlate with our inventory and escalate for immediate swap.

miguel_sre: After replacements are up, run these checks: 

```
# smoke validation
rwctl healthcheck --pool vortex-dedicated-01 --model redwood-small-quantized --tenant VortexSys --requests 100
rwctl perf --pool vortex-dedicated-01 --latency-target 150
```

miguel_sre: If smoke passes, we'll gradually shift traffic back from fallback to primary model using canary rollout (10% -> 50% -> 100%).

emma_oncall: Handoff note for next oncall (miguel_sre): keep provider ticket open, confirm hardware replacement or firmware patch, complete RCA. I'm going offline in ~10m but will stay reachable.

miguel_sre: Acknowledged. I'll take the handoff and post a post-incident ops checklist once things are stable.

olivia_support: Customer update sent at 11:49 UTC: "Replacements are provisioning; we expect normal routing restored within 30 minutes." VortexSys replied: "Thanks — appreciate the quick mitigation, please keep us posted."

emma_oncall: Final note before handoff: mark incident as 'mitigated' once canary back to 100% and error rate <0.1% for 5m. Also include billing credit for impacted window.

miguel_sre: Will do. Closing active ops log here, will publish RCA draft by EOD and postmortem with timeline + mitigations (prefer on-demand mix for enterprise pools, improve early-warning for ECC counter trends). :white_check_mark:
